mainTopic: Paying an expert examiner of a בכור, and why taking pay to judge, testify, or sprinkle the פרה אדומה water cancels the act
overview: The amud opens at the end of a משנה about paying an examiner of a בכור. An approved expert like אילא in יבנה may charge four איסרים for a small animal and six for a large one, and he is paid whether he finds it תם or בעל מום. The גמרא explains that a large animal takes more work to check. It also explains that he is paid either way so no one suspects him of inventing blemishes for money, and that he is paid only once per animal so he has no reason to delay. A new משנה rules that taking pay to judge, testify, or sprinkle and prepare the פרה אדומה water cancels the act. However, making up real losses, such as food for a כהן who became טמא, a ride for an old man, or lost work time, is allowed. The גמרא learns from משה רבינו that תורה is taught for free, and a ברייתא adds that one may pay to learn but never charge to teach. אביי resolves a contradiction with the משנה in קידושין: pay for carrying and filling is allowed, but pay for sprinkling and mixing is not. Finally, the גמרא explains that the כהן could have gone into a בית הפרס, which is only forbidden מדרבנן and may be crossed by blowing on the dust.

steps.title: אילא in יבנה may take a fixed wage
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the exception of אילא in יבנה. The חכמים allowed him a set fee for checking a בכור: four איסרים for a small animal and six for a large one. He is paid whether he finds it תם or בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like אילא in יבנה, whom the חכמים (in יבנה) allowed to take four איסרים for a small animal and six for a large animal, whether it is unblemished or blemished.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends its rule about paid examiners by naming the model of an approved expert: אילא in יבנה, with his allowed fees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, an examiner who takes money is not trusted, since money might push him to find a blemish. אילא is the exception: the חכמים approved his fee. The fee is fixed by animal size and paid no matter what he decides.

keyTerms.meaning: A recognized expert examiner of firstborn animals in יבנה
Unblemished, so it may not be slaughtered as ordinary food
Blemished, so it may be slaughtered and eaten

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole גמרא that follows: both the price difference and the 'paid either way' rule get explained.

phrases.english: like Ila in Yavne,
whom the Sages (in Yavne) permitted
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, since 'in Yavne' was already said.

phrases.english: to take four issar
for a small animal,
and six for a large one,
whether it is unblemished or blemished.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: An approved expert like אילא may take a fixed fee (4 for small, 6 for large) whether he finds the בכור תם or בעל מום.

steps.title: Why the different prices?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the fee is four for a small animal but six for a large one.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the different fees. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave two prices without explaining them. The גמרא wants to know what makes the large animal cost more.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why four for a small animal but six for a large one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the fee difference in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the large animal's fee is higher than the small animal's

steps.title: A large animal takes more work
steps.stepSummary: Checking a large animal for blemishes is more work, so the fee is higher.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one takes a lot of effort, and that one does not take a lot of effort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the fee matches the work, and a large animal is harder to examine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fee is payment for his labor, not for the ruling itself. A bigger animal needs more effort to inspect, so it earns a bigger fee.

phrases.english: this one takes a lot of effort,
and that one does not take a lot of effort.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fee matches the effort; a large animal takes more effort to examine.

steps.title: Why pay him for an unblemished animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'whether תם or בעל מום' and asks: paying for a בעל מום makes sense, since he permitted it. But why should he be paid when he finds it תם?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Whether unblemished or blemished.' Fine for blemished, because he permits it. But for unblemished, why?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that he is paid even when he finds no blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he finds a blemish, the owner gains something: he may now eat the animal. When he finds it תם, the owner gets nothing usable, so why should the owner pay?

phrases.english: 'Whether unblemished or blemished.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the end of the משנה from step 1.

phrases.english: It makes sense for a blemished one —
because he permits it,
but for an unblemished one, why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second detail of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that he is paid even for a תם animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Payment makes sense only when he gives the owner a benefit (permitting the animal); finding it תם gives no benefit.

steps.title: Otherwise people would suspect him
steps.stepSummary: If he were paid only for finding a blemish, people would suspect that he declares unblemished animals blemished just to get paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if so, people would suspect him and say: this 'blemished' animal is really unblemished, and he permitted it only for the wage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: paying him either way protects his trustworthiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the money depended on finding a blemish, every ruling of 'blemished' would look bought. Paying for both outcomes removes any reason to lean one way.

keyTerms.meaning: They will come to suspect him

phrases.english: Because if so, they would come to suspect him,
phrases.notes: 'If so' means: if he were paid only when he finds a blemish.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי: הַאי בַּעַל מוּם תָּם הוּא,
phrases.english: and say: this 'blemished' one is really unblemished,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי דְּקָא שָׁרֵי לֵיהּ — מִשּׁוּם אַגְרָא.
phrases.english: and the reason he permits it is because of the wage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Payment should be only for a benefit given, so only for finding a blemish
steps.terutzMaskana: Payment either way prevents people from suspecting he invents blemishes for money

steps.title: The same suspicion works the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: people could also suspect him when he says תם. Maybe it really has a blemish, and he calls it תם so he can be paid again when he examines it next time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, about an unblemished one they will also say: it is really blemished, and he did not permit it so that he can take his wage another time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 5 by showing that paying for 'תם' creates its own suspicion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said paying both ways removes the motive to lie. But if he gets paid for 'תם' now, he might say 'תם' so the owner brings it back later, and then he gets paid a second time.

phrases.english: If so, about an unblemished one they will also say:
it is really blemished,
and the reason he does not permit it

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלִשְׁקוֹל אַגְרֵיהּ זִימְנָא אַחֲרִיתִי!
phrases.english: is that he thinks: so that he can take his wage another time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that paying for both outcomes removes suspicion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Paying for a 'תם' ruling invites suspicion that he holds back a true blemish so he can be paid again on a later exam.

steps.title: He is paid only once per animal
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the רבנן set up payment for one examination only, not two. Calling it תם brings him no second fee, so he has no reason to lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן arranged for him to be paid one time; they did not arrange for him to be paid two times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the challenge: the rule allows one fee per animal, so there is nothing to gain by delaying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suspicion in step 6 only works if a second exam brings a second fee. Since the רבנן allowed just one payment per animal, saying 'תם' now cannot earn him more later. So he has no motive to lie either way.
steps.whatToRemember: The approved examiner gets one fixed fee per animal: more for a large animal (more work), and paid whether he finds תם or בעל מום, so he never has a money reason to rule either way.

phrases.english: The Sages arranged for him one time,

phrases.aramaic: תְּרֵי זִימְנֵי לָא תַּקִּינוּ לֵיה רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: two times the Sages did not arrange for him.
phrases.notes: He means one fee per animal; checking the same animal again earns nothing more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the scope of the enactment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could be paid on each examination, so delaying a ruling would earn more
steps.terutzMaskana: Payment is allowed only once per animal, so there is no gain in ruling it תם falsely

steps.title: Paid judges, witnesses, and purifiers make their acts worthless
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a judge or witness who takes pay voids his ruling or testimony, and one paid to sprinkle or prepare פרה אדומה water makes it plain water and plain ash.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who takes pay to judge: his rulings are void. Someone who takes pay to testify: his testimony is void. Someone who takes pay to sprinkle or to prepare the purifying water: his water is just cave water, and his ash is just ordinary burnt ash.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists jobs where taking pay ruins the act itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes further than 'it is forbidden.' The result is actually cancelled. The דין has no force, the עדות is not accepted, and the מי חטאת lose their power to purify.

keyTerms.meaning: To sprinkle the פרה אדומה water on someone impure from a dead body
To prepare the water by putting the פרה אדומה ash into it
Ordinary cave water, with no purifying power

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say the person merely did something wrong. It says the result itself has no legal value.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who takes his pay to judge
his rulings are void
to testify: his testimonies are void
to sprinkle and to sanctify
phrases.notes: Both are jobs with the פרה אדומה water used to purify someone who touched a dead body.

phrases.english: his water is cave water
his ash is burnt ash

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It widens the earlier topic of paying an examiner of a בכור to other jobs that may not be done for pay.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking pay to judge, testify, sprinkle, or prepare פרה אדומה water cancels the act.

steps.title: Covering real losses is allowed
steps.stepSummary: If the helper is a כהן who becomes unable to eat his תרומה, or an elderly man, the one who needs him must cover his food or his ride, and may pay him like a worker for lost time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was a כהן and became impure so he cannot eat his תרומה, the other person feeds him, gives him drink, and gives him oil. If he was old, the other person gives him a ride on a donkey. And he pays him his wage like a worker.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives permitted payments. They are not fees for the service. They cover what the helper loses by doing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pay for the act itself is forbidden, but making up a loss is fine. A כהן who becomes impure loses his תרומה food, so he gets regular food instead. Anyone can be paid what he would have earned from his usual work that day.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion a כהן eats, only while he is pure
Gives him oil to rub on his body
Like a worker, meaning pay for the work he missed

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that one may be paid for lost time and losses, but not for the judging or testifying itself.

phrases.english: If he was a כהן
and he made him impure, keeping him from his תרומה
he feeds him, gives him drink, and gives him oil
and if he was old
he gives him a ride on the donkey
and gives him his pay like a worker
phrases.notes: He is paid for the work he gave up that day, not for the service itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 8. Payment that only covers a loss is allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Compensation for real loss and lost work time is permitted.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a judge may not take pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question focuses on the first case, the judge. The גמרא wants a פסוק showing that judging and teaching תורה must be done for free.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 8's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a judge's ruling for pay is void.

steps.title: As משה taught for free, so must we
steps.stepSummary: רב brings the פסוק 'See, I have taught you': just as משה רבינו received the תורה for free, so must it be passed on for free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the פסוק says, 'See, I have taught you…' Just as I learned for free, so you must teach for free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. משה רבינו's free teaching is the model for every judge and teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה says he taught 'as ה׳ my God commanded me.' The דרשה reads this to mean he got it for free and gave it for free. Judging is applying תורה, so it falls under the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on, meaning the פסוק continues

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said
as the verse says
"See, I have taught you, etc."
just as I did it for free
so too, you must do it for free

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in דברים 4:5 teaches that תורה is passed on for free, just as משה received it.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא makes the same דרשה from the words 'as ה׳ my God commanded me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: 'As ה׳ my God commanded me.' Just as I did it for free, so you must do it for free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא points to the second half of the same פסוק, 'as ה׳ my God commanded me.' This shows that רב's teaching is already found in a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It is also taught this way
"As the Lord my God commanded me"
just as I did it for free
so too, you must do it for free

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב's teaching that תורה must be taught for free.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'as ה׳ my God commanded me' the same way.

steps.title: If no free teacher exists, pay to learn
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that if you cannot find a free teacher, you should pay to learn, from the פסוק 'Buy truth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that if he cannot find someone to teach him for free, he should learn by paying? The פסוק says, 'Buy truth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a new rule for the student. Not finding a free teacher is no excuse to stop learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on charging is placed on the teacher, not on the learner. The word 'buy' shows that paying to learn is proper when needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know

phrases.english: And from where do we know that if he did not find someone for free
he should learn by paying
The verse states: "Buy truth"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא moves from the teacher's duty to the student's duty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If no free teacher is available, one must pay to learn.

steps.title: Paying to learn does not allow charging to teach
steps.stepSummary: Someone who paid to learn may not charge to teach, because the פסוק says 'Buy truth and do not sell.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know he should not say, 'Just as I learned it for pay, I will teach it for pay'? The פסוק says, 'Buy truth and do not sell.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes off a possible excuse. Paying for your own learning does not allow you to charge others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think he can earn back what he spent. The end of the פסוק, 'and do not sell,' rules this out. Buying תורה is allowed, but selling it never is.
steps.whatToRemember: Teaching and judging תורה must be free, as משה received and gave it for free. A student may pay to learn if he must, but he may never charge to teach. Pay is allowed only to cover real losses or lost work time.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he should not say
Just as I learned it for pay
so too, I will teach it for pay
The verse states: "Buy truth and do not sell it"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on step 13. Paying to learn does not allow charging to teach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who paid to learn still may not charge to teach.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תורה may be bought when necessary, but never sold.

steps.title: The משנה: Paid sprinkling makes the waters worthless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: someone who takes pay to sprinkle or prepare the מי חטאת turns them into plain water and plain ash.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone takes pay to sprinkle or to prepare the purification water, his water is like ordinary cave water and his ash is like ordinary burnt ash.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה about the waters of the פרה אדומה. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like a judge may not take pay, someone who sprinkles or prepares the מי חטאת may not take pay either. If he does, the water and ash lose their status and cannot make anyone טהור. This makes it sound like no one may get any benefit at all from these waters.

keyTerms.meaning: to sprinkle the purification water on a טָמֵא person
here: to prepare the water by putting the ash into it
plain cave water, with no special status
plain burnt ash, with no special status

steps.confusionAlert: Here לְקַדֵּשׁ does not mean making קידושין. It means preparing the פרה אדומה water by mixing in the ash. In the next step the same root means making קידושין with a woman.

phrases.english: One who takes pay to sprinkle and to prepare the water:
his water is like cave water,
his ash is like plain burnt ash.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the משנה's line from step 8 about pay for sprinkling and preparing the פרה אדומה water, to set up a contradiction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking pay to sprinkle or prepare the מי חטאת makes the water and ash lose their special status.

steps.title: Contradiction: A man may make קידושין with purification water
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in קידושין says a man may make קידושין with מי חטאת or its ash, which suggests they have money value.
steps.simpleTranslation: They pointed out a contradiction: If someone makes קידושין with purification water or with purification ash, she is married, even if he is a regular ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another משנה that seems to say the opposite. If a man can make קידושין with these waters, they must have value that can be used for benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין needs something worth money. If the מי חטאת count as something of value, then it seems people may benefit from them. That clashes with our משנה, which says taking pay for them ruins them.

keyTerms.meaning: and they pointed out a contradiction
the purification water of the פָּרָה אֲדֻמָּה
a regular Jew, not a כֹּהֵן or לֵוִי

phrases.english: And they pointed out a contradiction:
One who makes קידושין with purification water or purification ash,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in קידושין 58a. Here the word means marrying a woman, not preparing the water.

phrases.english: she is married,
even though he is a regular Israelite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה just quoted with a different משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that no one may take pay or benefit for the מי חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קידושין only works with something of money value, so the מי חטאת must have value people can benefit from.

steps.title: אביי: Pay for carrying is allowed, pay for sprinkling is not
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the two משניות talk about different kinds of work: carrying and filling versus sprinkling and mixing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. Here it means pay for bringing and filling, and here it means pay for sprinkling and preparing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי settles the contradiction by saying each משנה talks about a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying the ash from far away and filling the container with water are just hard work, and you may get paid for them. So the man can make קידושין with the value of doing that work for her. Sprinkling and mixing in the ash are the holy steps themselves, and taking pay for those is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult; there is no contradiction
pay for bringing the ash or water

steps.whyThisMatters: It draws a line between ordinary work around a מצוה, which you may be paid for, and the מצוה act itself, which must be done for free.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult.
Here it means pay for bringing and filling,
phrases.notes: This first 'here' is the משנה in קידושין.

phrases.english: here it means pay for sprinkling and preparing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each משנה deals with a different type of work.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed both משניות talk about the same benefit from the מי חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: קידושין uses the value of carrying and filling, which is allowed. Our משנה forbids pay for sprinkling and mixing.

steps.title: The wording of both משניות supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the exact words of each משנה fit אביי's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact: here it says 'to sprinkle and to prepare,' and there it says 'one who makes קידושין with purification water and with purification ash.' Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אביי by pointing to the exact words of each משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה uses action words, 'to sprinkle and to prepare,' so it is talking about the holy acts. The קידושין משנה lists water and ash separately, which means they have not been mixed yet, so it is still at the carrying and filling stage. That fits אביי perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is also exact; it supports this
learn from it; this is proven

steps.whatToRemember: You may be paid for carrying the ash and filling the water, but not for sprinkling or mixing. The wording of both משניות proves this.

phrases.english: The wording is also exact,
since here it teaches 'to sprinkle and to prepare,'
and there it teaches
'one who makes קידושין with purification water and with purification ash,'
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer from the wording of the משניות.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's split between carrying and filling versus sprinkling and mixing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exact words of our משנה and of the משנה in קידושין.

steps.title: The משנה: A כהן who was made טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if the examiner was a כהן and was made טמא so he cannot eat his תרומה, he must be given food.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was a כהן and they made him טמא so he could not eat his תרומה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. This sets up a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a judge or examiner may not be paid. But if he is a כהן and the job made him טמא so that he loses his תרומה food, the person who needed him must give him food, drink and oil. The 'and so on' points to the rest of that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion of crops given to a כֹּהֵן; he may eat it only while טָהוֹר
and so on; the rest of the quote

phrases.english: If he was a priest
and he made him impure, keeping him from his תרומה, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: he must then give the כהן food, drink and oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who is made טמא for the job and loses his תרומה must be given food.

steps.title: How could the כהן go somewhere that made him טמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the כהן was allowed to go to a place that made him טמא in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He himself, how could he go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the משנה just quoted. A כהן is not allowed to make himself טמא, so how could he go?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to describe a כהן going to a place where he became טמא. A כהן may not make himself טמא from a dead body. So the גמרא wants to know how this case could be allowed at all.

phrases.english: He himself, how could he go?
phrases.notes: He means: a כהן may not make himself טמא, so how was he allowed to go there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the case in the משנה could happen.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of a כהן who becomes טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן is forbidden to make himself טמא, so it seems he should never have gone there.

steps.title: He went into a field that is only forbidden by the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the כהן went into a בית הפרס, which is only forbidden to a כהן מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to a בית הפרס, which is only a rabbinic matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20 about how the כהן could go to a place that would make him טמא. It says he went into a בית הפרס, which is only forbidden מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 assumed the כהן did something forbidden by going where he could become טמא. The answer is that a בית הפרס is not a place of definite טומאה from the תורה. It is only a rabbinic concern, so the rules for entering it can be easier.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed up, so bones may be scattered. No one knows exactly where they are.
From the Rabbis, not directly from the תורה

phrases.english: To a בית הפרס, which is rabbinic,
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out 'he went'. It means the כהן went into this kind of field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the place he went is only rabbinically forbidden.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן went somewhere forbidden to him מדאורייתא, which he should not have done.
steps.terutzMaskana: He went into a בית הפרס, which is only a rabbinic restriction, so there is room to allow it.

steps.title: You may blow on the ground and walk through a בית הפרס
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says a person may blow on the dust of a בית הפרס and keep walking. This shows a כהן is allowed to enter one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person may blow on a בית הפרס and walk on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up step 21. רב says a person may walk through a בית הפרס if he blows on the ground as he goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a בית הפרס is only rabbinic, the Rabbis gave an easy way to check it. You blow away the dust in front of you, and any bone underneath will show. Since a כהן may enter this way, it makes sense that the כהן in the משנה was allowed to go there.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהן was allowed to go because a בית הפרס is only forbidden מדרבנן. He may walk through it by blowing on the ground as he goes.

phrases.english: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
A person may blow on a בית הפרס and walk on.
phrases.notes: He blows the dust in front of each step. If a bone is hidden there, it will show up and he can step around it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 21 with a known ruling
steps.raayaObject: That a כהן may go into a בית הפרס
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב: a person may blow on a בית הפרס and walk on
